data.reason:
- Install approved application <Application Name> on endpoint <Device Name>
- Application is part of the standard service catalogue
- Required to support normal business activities
data.steps:
- Verify approved service request for <Application Name>
- Confirm <Device Name> meets application prerequisites
- Deploy <Application Name> version <Version No> using standard deployment method <Intune/Manual/Other>
- Apply default configuration as per service catalogue
- Confirm installation completed successfully
data.testPlan:
- Verify <Application Name> is installed on <Device Name>
- Launch application to confirm it opens successfully
- Confirm no errors are logged post-install
data.risks:
- Installation may fail due to device configuration issues
- Minor user disruption during install window
- No expected impact to other users or services
data.securityRisks:
- Low risk
- Application is approved and vetted via service catalogue
- No additional privileges or access changes introduced
data.backupPlan:
- Uninstall <Application Name> if installation fails or causes issues
- Restore device to pre-install state if required
- Reattempt installation after resolving any identified issues
data.expectedResults:
- <Application Name> is successfully installed on <Device Name>
- Application functions as expected
- No negative impact to endpoint stability or security

data.reason:
- Remove user access for <Forename> <Surname> from <Organisation>
- User no longer requires access from <Access Removal Date>
- Reason for access removal: <Reason>
- This is a repeatable, low-risk, pre-approved offboarding activity
data.steps:
- Verify approved request for access removal and effective date <Access Removal Date>
- Disable or remove primary identity account in the IdP
- Remove access from the following systems and services:
  - <Systems/Apps>
- Remove user from security and distribution groups
- Disable or archive mailbox and user data as per policy
- Record completion for audit purposes
- Notify requester once access removal is complete
data.testPlan:
- Confirm IdP account is disabled or removed
- Verify user no longer has access to listed systems
- Confirm group memberships are removed
- Validate mailbox and login access are no longer available
data.risks:
- Delayed removal could result in unauthorised access
- Incorrect removal may impact business continuity if timing is wrong
- No expected impact to other users or services
data.securityRisks:
- Low risk when completed on the correct date
- Reduces risk of unauthorised access by removing credentials
- No new access or privileges introduced
data.backupPlan:
- Re-enable account temporarily if removal is performed in error
- Restore group memberships or access if required
- Escalate immediately if access is removed prematurely
data.expectedResults:
- <Forename> <Surname> no longer has access from <Access Removal Date>
- All specified systems and services are removed as requested
- User access complies with organisational offboarding and security policies

data.reason:
- Provision a privileged user account for <Forename> <Surname>
- Account is required to perform authorised administrative duties in the <Privileged Role> role for <Organisation>
- This follows an approved, repeatable privileged access provisioning process
data.steps:
- Verify approved request and business justification for privileged access
- Create separate privileged account (not the user’s standard account)
- Assign the <Privileged Role> role
- Apply least-privilege permissions aligned to the role
- Enforce security controls (e.g. MFA, password policy, conditional access)
- Record account and role assignment for audit purposes
- Notify requester once provisioning is complete
data.testPlan:
- Confirm privileged account exists and is enabled
- Verify <Privileged Role> permissions are correctly applied
- Confirm access works for intended administrative tasks only
- Validate security controls (e.g. MFA enforcement)
data.risks:
- Misconfiguration could result in excessive privileges
- Potential security exposure if account is not adequately protected
- No expected impact to end users or live services
data.securityRisks:
- Elevated risk due to privileged access
- Risk mitigated by separate account, role-based assignment, and enforced security controls
- No access beyond the approved <Privileged Role> - Role has been reviewed and principle of least privilege is applied.
data.backupPlan:
- Immediately disable or remove the privileged account if issues are identified
- Remove <Privileged Role> assignment if incorrect
- Recreate account following corrected approval if required
data.expectedResults:
- Privileged account for <Forename> <Surname> is active
- <Privileged Role> access is correctly assigned and restricted
- Account complies with organisational privileged access security standards

data.reason:
- Provision a new user account for <Forename> <Surname>
- User requires access to corporate systems to perform the <Role> role at <Organisation>
- This is a repeatable, low-risk, pre-approved onboarding activity
data.steps:
- Verify approved user request for <Forename> <Surname>
- Create user account in directory service as per <Organisation> procedure.
- Assign standard role-based access for <Role>
- Add user to required security and distribution groups
- Configure mailbox and basic account settings
- Notify requester and any other stakeholders once account creation is complete
data.testPlan:
- Confirm user account exists and is enabled
- Verify correct group and role assignments as per request form received
- Confirm mailbox, application and login access function as expected
data.risks:
- User may receive incorrect access if role details are wrong
- Minor administrative rework if changes are required post-creation
- No expected impact to existing users or services
data.securityRisks:
- Low risk
- Access granted is limited to standard role-based permissions
- No elevated or privileged access assigned
data.backupPlan:
- Disable or remove the user account if created incorrectly
- Roll back group memberships to default state
- Recreate account if provisioning fails
data.expectedResults:
- <Forename> <Surname> has an active user account
- Correct access is in place for the <Role> role
- User is able to access required systems for <Organisation>

data.reason:
- Add a standard firewall policy to allow <Application Name> network access
- Required to support normal business operation of the application
- Change follows an approved, repeatable firewall rule process
data.steps:
- Verify approved request and policy details for <Application Name>
- Create new firewall policy with the following parameters:
  - Policy Name: <Policy Name>
  - Source Interface: <Source Interface>
  - Destination Interface: <Destination Interface>
  - Source IPs: <Source IPs>
  - Destination IPs: <Destination IPs>
  - Services / Ports: <Services>
- Apply standard logging and security profiles
- Position rule according to firewall policy standards
- Commit and deploy configuration
data.testPlan:
- Confirm firewall policy is present and enabled
- Verify <Application Name> can reach intended destination
- Confirm no unintended traffic is permitted
- Review firewall logs for expected traffic
data.risks:
- Incorrect rule configuration could block required traffic
- Overly permissive settings could allow unintended access
- No expected impact to other services when correctly scoped
data.securityRisks:
- Low risk if rule follows least-privilege principles
- Risk increases if IP ranges or services are too broad
- No inbound access permitted unless explicitly defined
data.backupPlan:
- Disable or remove the firewall policy if issues occur
- Roll back firewall configuration to last known good state
- Reapply corrected rule following review
data.expectedResults:
- Firewall policy <Policy Name> is active
- <Application Name> can access required network destinations
- No unintended access or disruption to existing traffic

data.reason:
- Increase disk capacity for virtual machine <VM Name>
- Existing disk <Disk Identifier> requires additional space to support normal operations
- This is a repeatable, low-risk VMware disk expansion activity
data.steps:
- Confirm approved request and required additional disk size <Additional Disk Size>
- Log in to vCenter
- Locate virtual machine <VM Name>
- Edit VM settings and expand disk <Disk Identifier> by <Additional Disk Size>
- Confirm disk change is applied successfully in vCenter
- Log in to <VM Name> (Windows)
- Open Disk Management
- Rescan disks
- Extend the relevant volume to use the newly allocated space
- Confirm disk expansion completes successfully
data.testPlan:
- Pre-change:
  - Confirm current disk usage on <VM Name>
  - Verify available free space on datastore <Datastore Name>: <Available Datastore Space>
- Post-vCenter change:
  - Confirm disk size is increased at VM level
- Post-OS change:
  - Verify volume is expanded in Windows Disk Management
  - Confirm available free space is visible within the OS
  - Validate application or service functionality if applicable
data.risks:
- Disk expansion may fail if datastore space is insufficient
- Incorrect disk selection could impact the wrong volume
- Minimal risk to services when correct disk is identified
data.securityRisks:
- Low risk
- No access, permissions, or exposure changes introduced
- Change limited to storage capacity only
data.backupPlan:
- Do not proceed if datastore space is insufficient
- Revert disk size change if vCenter expansion fails
- Restore from backup or snapshot if disk corruption occurs
- Escalate to virtualization team if rollback is required
data.expectedResults:
- Disk <Disk Identifier> on <VM Name> is successfully expanded
- Additional space <Additional Disk Size> is available within Windows
- No impact to system stability or security
